title: Is the Continuum Hypothesis decided by large cardinal axioms

problemStatement.plain: Is the Continuum Hypothesis decided by large cardinal axioms?.

currentState.focus: Formalized large cardinal axioms, Lévy-Solovay independence, and proved MM/MA → ¬CH.

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS (Session 1, 2026-05-03): Formalized large cardinal axioms (inaccessible, measurable), forcing axioms (Martin's Axiom, Martin's Maximum), Lévy-Solovay independence results (axiomatized), and proved MM→¬CH, MA→¬CH by cardinal arithmetic. 11 theorems, 6 axioms, 0 sorries.

insights: Standard large cardinals (measurable, supercompact) don't decide CH — Lévy-Solovay: small forcing preserves measurability
Martin's Maximum implies 2^ℵ₀ = ℵ₂, which provably contradicts CH (2^ℵ₀ = ℵ₁) since ℵ₁ < ℵ₂
Martin's Axiom implies 2^ℵ₀ ≥ ℵ₂, similarly refuting CH
Woodin Ultimate-L program aims to canonically settle CH as true using inner model theory — still open
The key distinction: 'size' axioms (large cardinals) don't decide CH; 'saturation' axioms (forcing axioms) do
Cardinal.aleph_lt.mpr (by norm_num) is the clean way to prove aleph α < aleph β from α < β
mathlibGaps: No Mathlib formalization of measurable cardinals (Scott's theorem, ultrafilters on cardinals)
Forcing is not formalized in Mathlib — Lévy-Solovay must be axiomatized
nextSteps: Extension: add GCH → CH consequence to show GCH is a stronger axiom
